title: Sparse array of maps: cells grow quadratically and values move to the wrong element
rationale: The real "more output than input" case and the most serious defect in this family. One column per distinct field across all elements means output cells scale as fields x elements while maxArraySize bounds only the element count. Worse, padding appends nulls to the END of each short column instead of inserting at the absent element index.
catchesBugClass: Positional information destroyed by columnar flattening of heterogeneous array elements; padding that equalises length without preserving index; absent-key-becomes-present-null inside array elements; and output-size growth that no configured bound constrains.
cannotCatch: Uniform arrays never trigger it, which is why it survived. It also cannot quantify the blowup at this size; a wider variant is needed to make the quadratic growth measurable.

predicted.detail: Every sparse value is RELOCATED into element 0 and the later elements are emptied. Not loss - silent corruption that reads as valid data. Every element also gains explicit nulls for keys it never had.
